ruleName: SaaS billing page: a "?" help button beside "Seat overage" shows a custom tooltip positioned 30px BELOW the trigger, separated by a transparent .gap spacer (pointer-events:none). Moving the pointer down to read the tooltip crosses the gap, fires mouseout, and the tooltip vanishes before the pointer reaches it.

Community forum thread: a GitHub/Twitter-style profile "hover card" appears when hovering a username. It is rendered into a detached portal layer (#hovercard-layer, sibling of the content) positioned 12px below the username. Moving the pointer down to the card crosses the 12px transparent gap, fires mouseleave, and the card vanishes instantly.

Pharmacy prescription page: a glossary term <dfn> ("contraindication") shows a definition pop-up that DIRECTLY overlaps/adjoins the term (top:-2px, no gap) — visually the passing arrangement the Understanding describes. But the pop-up carries pointer-events:none and reveal is keyed only to the term's :hover, so moving the pointer onto the pop-up means the cursor is no longer counted as over the term, :hover collapses, and the content vanishes. Adjacency is present but the content is not actually hoverable.

Cloud-platform status console with a 'Region health' matrix where each region/service state (operational/degraded/major outage) is shown only by the hue of an identically-shaped green/amber/red dot. Ledgerline invoicing toolbar: every button (Save/Export/Send/Duplicate) carries only a native title= attribute (e.g. title='Save your work'). The tooltip is adjacent/overlapping (4px overlap, no gap), has pointer-events:auto and its own mouseenter, a 120ms hide delay tolerates the sub-element transition, and Esc dismisses it. A continuous pointer path from button to tooltip keeps the content visible.

Patient-portal medication list: an 'interactions' pill on Warfarin opens a drug-interaction warning box that covers the dosage text. Online-banking transfer-limit screen: a round 'i' info button shows a tooltip on hover AND keyboard focus that overlaps the help paragraph and the Continue button. The tooltip is keyboard-reachable (meets 2.1.1) but there is NO Escape handler, no documented shortcut, and activating the trigger does not toggle it off — the only way to clear the obscuring content is to move focus/pointer off the trigger.

SaaS analytics dashboard: a '?' badge on a conversion KPI opens a definition popover that covers the device-breakdown list. The popover is hoverable and persistent, but its only dismiss affordance is a close '×' button positioned INSIDE the popover, reachable only by Tab-ing focus off the trigger and into the additional content. RTL (Arabic) API-reference docs: a dotted-underline glossary term 'cursor' shows a hover-only tooltip on a non-focusable span that covers the curl example block. E-commerce (outdoor retail) product 'Quick view' modal (role=dialog aria-modal=true). A focus trap cycles Tab among the size/quantity/Add-to-cart controls. The only dismiss is a round '✕' that is a <span> with role=button + aria-label and an onclick handler only — not focusable (no tabindex, not a real button) and with no keydown; there is also no Esc handler. Closeable by mouse, trapped by keyboard.

Government public-library 'Renew library card' modal. Focus is contained (Tab cycles inside), there is NO advice text and the close control is labelled 'Cancel' not 'Esc', but pressing Esc dismisses the dialog and restores focus to the trigger. A naive checker sees a focus cycle with no documented exit and wrongly flags a trap; it actually passes because Esc is a standard exit method, so no advice is owed.

Healthcare patient-portal refill modal built with native <dialog open>: a JS focus trap cycles Tab among the refill form's four controls, but there is no Close/Cancel control and no Esc handler. Because the dialog was rendered with the open attribute (not opened via showModal()) the UA's native Esc-cancel is not armed either; only a mouse backdrop-click escapes. Keyboard users are stranded.

Arrows move between tabs and Tab is NOT preventDefault'd, but each tab has a blur listener that refocuses the active tab on the next tick (setTimeout(()=>tab.focus())), so pressing Tab to leave the tablist toward the panel link or the Export button instantly snaps focus back to the tab.

Job-application form with a roving-tabindex role=listbox ('How did you hear about this role?'). Arrows navigate options and Enter selects; the keydown handler deliberately omits any Tab case, so unmodified Tab carries focus OUT to the Submit button and Shift+Tab back to the Email field. The on-screen help wrongly says 'Use Tab to move between options' — a misleading mental model, but NOT a 2.1.2 failure because Tab still exits. Boundary PASS case.

Theatre box-office seat-picker modal (Aurora Hall). Both Esc and Close release focus, but the promo-code <input> calls stopPropagation() on its keydown, so Escape never reaches the dialog handler WHEN that field is focused. Esc works from the seat buttons and silently fails from the input — a positional trap that requires testing exit from EACH focus position.

RTL Arabic article-publishing editor with an APG role=toolbar (Bold/Italic/Underline/List/Link) using roving tabindex and aria-pressed toggles. In RTL, ArrowLeft advances; the handler also captures Tab and the movement WRAPS, so at the last button advancing loops back to the first instead of exiting — a closed within-widget loop with no exit index. The title field and Publish button are unreachable. No Esc, no instruction.

E-commerce headphones store with a custom div role=slider 'Max price' facet. Arrows (and PageUp/Down, Home/End) adjust the price with complete ARIA value semantics, but the thumb keydown handler also captures Tab with preventDefault() 'to prevent accidental value loss when you tab away mid-drag', with no Esc and no instruction, so focus is stranded on the thumb and cannot reach Apply, the brand checkboxes, or the product links.

Public-library account-signup form: a required email field suppresses a plain forward Tab while the value is not a valid e-mail (so it LOOKS like a trap), then releases focus to the password field, submit button and rest of the page the instant a valid address is typed by keyboard.
